key_insight: The paper proves that random-reshuffling SGD can achieve last-iterate convergence with a much larger constant stepsize, removing the usual explicit 1/n dependence and keeping only a logarithmic penalty in the number of epochs and components.
engineering_relevance: This makes RR-SGD more practical for machine learning training loops where the final model iterate is what matters and stepsize tuning should not need to shrink with dataset size.
method: Analyzes unconstrained finite-sum optimization with convex, L-smooth component functions.
Keeps the sampling bias at random comparison points instead of averaging it away, which enables the improved stepsize condition.
Derives an expected objective-gap bound for the final iterate with eta up to order 1/(L(1+log(nK))).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an expected objective-gap bound and states that, when combined with existing small-step results, the new rate matches averaged-iterate convergence up to logarithmic factors.
watch_item: The guarantee still depends on a logarithmic factor in nK, so the practical benefit may diminish for very large datasets or long training runs if stepsizes are pushed too aggressively.
paper_title: Large-Step Last-Iterate Convergence of Random-Reshuffling Stochastic Gradient Descent
